findings.finding: The stale-editor check must go in the token path. The Hocuspocus Auth token decision replaces the upgrade-time query decision in both directions. An old bundle always sends token=String(fetchedVersion). If the server checks a new capability only on the query, authorizeSchemaVersion admits an old bundle that presents token "<new N>" read-write, and the fence is bypassed. So the signal an old bundle cannot present has to be a token format and a query parameter that old code never emits, for example a new query field plus a new token shape. Echoing a fetched value is not enough.
findings.answer: Decision 3 and step 5: new query field editor_schema and token '<schema>:<editor>' from the compiled contracts constant DOCUMENT_EDITOR_SCHEMA_VERSION; schemaReadOnly requires both in authorize and authorizeSchemaVersion; one docstest helper updates every writing dialer (docs/websocket_test.go:30, api/browser_peer_test.go:87, api/storable_text_test.go:706, cmd/dispatch/memory_harness_test.go:348, cmd/dispatch/shutdown_test.go:694); websocket_test table covers old/new query and token shapes and asserts both the upgrade decision and the auth scope.

findings.finding: A4's gates cannot catch the new failures. The engine is run from the working tree for both revisions, so every document with a linked image makes base 'incorrect'. Two failures therefore pass every gate today: head disagreeing with the engine on a linked image, for example on emphasis, whitespace or table-cell shapes, and head refusing a write base takes. findings.finding: Pasting into the editor uses toDOM and parseDOM, not only the markdown reader. Milkdown's clipboard plugin parses a text/plain markdown paste with the markdown parser, serializes the result with DOMSerializer (toDOM), and re-parses that DOM with DOMParser.parseSlice (parseDOM). An HTML paste, including a copy and paste inside the editor, goes through parseDOM directly. Milkdown's image parseDOM reads only src/alt/title, and its toDOM spreads every attr onto . The link mark's `a[href]` rule then puts a mark on the image, and y-prosemirror drops that mark. So with only a markdown reader, a pasted linked image loses its link at the next reload. If parseDOM reads the link and the `a[href]` mark rule still fires, the image carries both the attr and a mark in the session, and the clipboard text serializer writes `[[![x](i)](u)](u)`. Also, the planner's note 'Dispatch web never calls serializeMarkdown' is wrong: clipboardTextSerializer calls serializerCtx on every copy.
findings.answer: Step 2: image toDOM wraps in a sanitized ; parseDOM reads the data attributes or a parent whose only child is the img; linkSchema's a[href] rule skips such an anchor so no link mark doubles; tests cover text/plain paste through handlePaste, HTML copy-paste and external paste.

findings.finding: 'opens ... as a text link does' does not settle every view and link kind, and some combinations do not open today. (a) Read-only view: VersionView sits outside the <article> whose onClick navigates dispatch:// links. markdownLinkClickPlugin returns false for an empty href (a sanitized dispatch:// link), so a dispatch:// link, text or image, opens nothing in a past version today. (b) Editable live document: dispatch:// text links open on a plain click through the article handler, which returns when the DOM selection is not collapsed. A click on a selectable atom image makes a NodeSelection, so [INFERENCE] a plain click on a dispatch://-linked image will not navigate unless the handler changes. Also, Ctrl/Cmd-click on a dispatch:// link goes to the plugin, which refuses href "". (c) 'the read-only view' could mean a past version (VersionView) or a closed issue's live editor (inside the article).

findings.finding: Wrapping a Dispatch picture in its link nests anchors, or empties the outer one. In comments, pictureSerializer turns a pinned picture into `<a data-dispatch-picture href=artifact page>`. Under an outer link, a click hits the inner anchor, so the image's own link never opens. An unpinned picture, or one that fails to load, renders RefLink, another anchor. collectReferenceAnchors matches every a:not([data-dispatch-picture]) whose target is dispatch:// or a same-origin Dispatch URL, and calls replaceChildren(). An outer dispatch:// link around an image therefore loses the image, against A3's 'with the picture still shown'. In documents, the fallback link (unpinned picture, or img error) would sit inside the outer anchor.
findings.answer: Decision 6 and step 6: a linked Dispatch picture opens the image's link; inside a link its placeholder and fallback are spans (no nested anchors); collectReferenceAnchors keeps the children of an anchor holding an img or picture placeholder while still rewriting its href; unit tests in MarkdownBody.test.tsx and picture-view.test.ts.

Order: in the browser, commonmark's remark-inline-links (lib.ts:295) runs before dispatchMarks (:315); in the headless pipeline it runs after (lib-headless.ts:130-141). The new transform must run after both, in both. Ask spans: renderInlineNode prints link `[text](href)` and image `![alt](src)` without titles, so a linked image in an Ask span loses both titles on the TS side. inlineSignature ignores image attrs, so runReadsBack cannot c

findings.finding: A5 says neither how a machine checks 'an editor built before the change', nor that 'no edit it sends removes an image's link'. It also misses one path. The IndexedDB pending store keeps every local Yjs update, from any client ID, across reloads. On the first writable admission it replays every row for the document, judging rows only for 'parking', not content. So rows an old bundle stored are sent later by a new bundle, possibly from another tab in the same browser, which A5's 'edit it sends' does not cover. [INFERENCE] The risk is low: a read-only old editor cannot edit an image, rows saved before the deploy predate any link attribute, and y-prosemirror rewrites only image nodes that actually changed. The plan should argue this or test it.
